independent exact pair-first and union-first census
correctness.rationale: An independent exact anonymous-profile enumeration used the three pairwise majority margins to compute maximin winners. The pair-first traversal found no reinforcement pair for total electorate sizes \(2\) through \(14\), and exactly \(18\) at total size \(15\), all with split \(5+10\). An independently organized union-first decomposition of every 15-voter profile returned the identical set. Canonicalization under all six candidate relabelings gave three pair classes of size six, all 18 unions were distinct with exactly one paradox-producing partition, and every witness had the claimed Condorcet-status pattern.
residual_risks: The theorem is finite and computational, but two independently organized exact traversals agree on the full witness set.

evidence: The 2022 open full article gives the systematic minimal-instance framework and treats reinforcement for maximin among 13 voting rules.
The later three-candidate work studies rule-level reinforcement and refinements rather than enumerating every ordinary-maximin boundary witness.

inspection of the 2022 minimal-paradox article's stated notion of completeness

originality.rationale: Brandt-Matthäus-Saile's open primary article systematically computes minimal paradox instances and explicitly treats maximin reinforcement, so the voter boundary itself is not new. However, the article defines completeness as supplying a minimal-voter instance and a minimal-candidate instance; it does not state an exhaustive count of every minimal anonymous witness. Targeted searches found no prior \(18\)-pair, three-orbit, unique-union-partition census, and Resultary returned no equivalent finding.
residual_risks: Supplementary code or an unindexed thesis may have generated and retained the same complete witness set even though the checked publication does not state it.

value.rationale: Reinforcement is a standard consistency axiom and maximin is a canonical Condorcet procedure. Completing the first possible three-candidate boundary from one known minimal witness to the full 18-pair set, symmetry quotient, unique partition property, and Condorcet-status structure is a natural exact finite classification.
residual_risks: Tie-dependent outcomes and four-or-more-candidate markets are outside scope.

limitations: Exactly three candidates, strict complete anonymous ballots, and unique maximin winners are assumed.
